{ff02}Baccarat uses 13 kinds of cards:
A, 2 to 10, J, Q and K. A counts
as 1; 10, J, Q and K count as 0.{ff01}{ff02}It's BANKER versus PLAYER.
You bet on which one
will win.{ff01}{ff02}Each side draws up to 3 cards
and compares the total.{ff01}{ff02}A total of 9 is best. The closer
to 9, the stronger the hand.{ff01}{ff02}10 counts as 0, 11 as 1, 12 as 2,
13 as 3... and so on.{ff01}{ff02}First, 2 cards each are dealt.
Whether to draw a third is set
by rules for the best odds.{ff01}{ff02}PLAYER goes first on the third
card: draw on 5 or less,
stand on 6 or more.{ff01}{ff02}BANKER draws on 2 or less; on 3 to 6,
it looks at PLAYER's third card.
It stands on 7.{ff01}{ff02}A two-card 8 or 9 is a NATURAL.
Then nobody draws a third card;
the two-card totals decide it.{ff01}{ff02}Pick a side with Up/Down. Raise
your bet with Circle or Triangle,
lower it with X or Square.{ff01}{ff02}You can bet BANKER and TIE, or
PLAYER and TIE, together,
but not B and P together.{ff01}{ff02}Once your bet is set, press R1 to
start, then R1 to advance.
Press L1 when you want to stop.{ff01}{ff02}BANKER has a slight edge, so if
you bet on BANKER and win,
we take 5 percent.{ff01}{ff02}On a tie, your coins are returned.
If you bet on TIE, your bet
pays 9 times.{ff01}{ff02}RESULT shows past results.
Following them to make your call
is the fun of Baccarat.{ff01}{ff02}Now, please enjoy yourself.{ff01}
